# ADR-002 — Lexicon-anchored tone Beta rule and verification principles (D6 / C2)

Status: **Accepted** (Tope, 2026-10-21). Records decision D6 (tone Beta rule) and closes CONFLICTS C2.

## Context

Elevation §6.2 and §7.4 require that tone and diacritics are never “AI-only.” The Curriculum plan (§3.4, §6) allows **Beta** labels for machine-verified output when tone marks are **lexicon-anchored** and pass **three-way agreement** (lexicon form = generator surface = restorer output). CONFLICTS C2 reconciles these positions: agreed, anchored marks are not AI-only; unmatched or unanchored marks are not publishable as Beta.

ADR-001 defines the three verification labels. This ADR defines **when tone-bearing tokens may ship as Beta** and the **generation and review principles** every content item must satisfy.

## Decision

### Tone marks and Beta (C2)

| Condition | Route | Label cap |
|---|---|---|
| Tone or teaching diacritic on a token **with lexicon anchor** and **three-way agreement** (`tone_agreement.py`) | May auto-publish when confidence routing allows | **Beta** (subject to ADR-001 exclusions) |
| Tone mark **without lexicon anchor** (`matched` false or empty anchor) | **Hard failure** — 100% to linguist queue; no Beta auto-publish | — |
| **Tone teaching notes** (explanatory copy about tone, not surface tokens) | Human review required | **Expert-reviewed minimum** — **never Beta** |

Three-way agreement uses the language kit restorer when configured (`restorer.py`, `CONTENT_ENGINE_NAIJAML_MODEL` per EXT-01); kits with `tone_restorer: none` use two-way lexicon/generator agreement only where the kit permits.

Unmatched tone tokens route to linguist review with stable failure codes from the tone-claim linter (CP-§3.3); they do not pass as “machine verified.”

### Generation principles (every item)

Each generated or rebuilt item must:

1. **Cite sources claim-by-claim** in schema (`claims[]`, passages, licence ids) — no invented linguistic facts.
2. **Cross-check** with a second model family (`crosscheck.py`).
3. **Back-translate** and compare (`backtranslate.py`; MT routing cites EXT-01).
4. **Run deterministic linters** per language (`stage_lint.py`); hard failures reject or route to linguist, not silent pass.
5. **Carry a calibrated confidence score** (`scoring.py`, `calibration.py`) on the item.

Model and vendor choices are recorded in `docs/plan/LINGAFRIQ_AI_MODEL_STACK.md` (EXT-01). Intron and ZulMorph stay off behind flags. No AI keys in client apps.

### Confidence routing (§3.4)

After linters and scoring (`routing.py`, P4-064):

| Score band (calibrated) | Linter gates | Route | Label |
|---|---|---|---|
| **High** (≥ 0.90) | All planned linters pass; no high-risk tags | `publish_beta` | **Beta** |
| **Mid** (≥ 0.70, &lt; 0.90) or high-risk tags present | — | `linguist` / human queue | None until reviewed |
| **Low** (&lt; 0.70) or hard linter failure | — | `regenerate` then `human_park` at cap | None — reject and regenerate |

High-risk tags (`highrisk.py`) force linguist review even when score is high; they cannot publish with a Beta label.

### Expert spot-checks (D4)

- **100% review** of high-risk classes: tone marks without lexicon match, idioms, culture and history, honorifics, grammar explanations.
- **Statistical sample** of remaining Beta-bound items per calibration policy.
- **Owners**: two part-time linguists per Stage-1 language with consent and IP clause (**D4**; procurement **EXT-11**).

### Lexicon and tooling prerequisites (D2, D5)

| Prerequisite | Decision | External card |
|---|---|---|
| Oxford datasets (yo, ig, ha, xh; sw via API) | Approved (D2) | **EXT-04** |
| IgboAPI (Nkọwa okwu) | Approved (D2) | **EXT-05** |
| isiZulu dictionary licence | Approved (D2) | **EXT-06** |
| Curriculum Studio in `lingafriq-admin` | Approved (D5) | Studio / P4 cards |

Purchases and contracts remain blocked until quotes and sign-off complete; pipeline code must **gate** on licence register rows, not assume holdings.

### Licence register (legal reading)

Commercial licence summaries in planning docs are a **product-manager reading** pending **counsel sign-off** of the licence register (**EXT-03**). No card treats PM notes as legal advice.

## Verification (conformance checks for later cards)

| Check | Where enforced |
|---|---|
| Three-way tone agreement | `tone_agreement.py`, `test_tone_agreement.py` |
| Unanchored tone hard failure | Tone-claim linter, `native_validation` |
| Tone teaching notes never Beta | Schema + review workflow |
| Cross-check / back-translate / linters | `crosscheck.py`, `backtranslate.py`, `stage_lint.py` |
| Confidence routing table | `routing.py`, `test_routing.py` |
| High-risk 100% + Beta block | `highrisk.py`, `test_highrisk.py` |
| Publish gate | `publish.py` |
